identity.description:
Pin the ten D5 cases and write the first baseline

## What

- `eval/cases.json` points at jerridan/pr-review-cases main c86b210, the ten labeled cases of D5.
- `eval/baseline.json`: recall 0.287, precision 0.636, one repeat, margins 0.10 and 0.35 as before. Written by hand from the report of the run below, because the eval refuses to write a baseline when a repeat fails and one case failed.
- Section 8 of the design records the local eval practice. TICKETS.md marks the D5 labeling and pin bullets done and adds a D6 bullet for the failure.

## The eval run, 2026-11-08, one repeat

| Case | Recall | Precision | Posted | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| martian-calcom-8330 | 1.000 | 0.500 | 4 | $9.02 |
| martian-discourse-graphite-1 | failed | | | |
| martian-sentry-93824 | 0.250 | 1.000 | 1 | $5.66 |
| martian-sentry-greptile-1 | 1.000 | 0.600 | 5 | $11.62 |
| reviewbench-axios-10836 | 0.000 | - | 0 | $2.01 |
| reviewbench-claire-de-binare-1550 | 0.000 | - | 0 | $1.97 |
| reviewbench-disaster-ninja-fe-1166 | 0.000 | - | 0 | $1.72 |
| reviewbench-ensnode-1938 | 0.333 | 1.000 | 1 | $0.89 |
| reviewbench-flatten-js-244 | 0.000 | - | 0 | $2.45 |
| reviewbench-statswales-frontend-626 | 0.000 | - | 0 | $2.87 |
| mean over nine | 0.287 | 0.636 | 1.22 | $4.25 |

The discourse case failed whole: the Opus escalation of one finding in a 1000-line locale file reached its $1 budget, and the review reported itself incomplete. D6 gets a bullet: a budget stop gives that finding `unsure` and the review completes.

Five ReviewBench cases posted nothing. Cost per case is $4.25 against $0.6 to $1.4 in D1. Both are the numbers behind issue #18.

finding.claim: The precision margin of 0.35 on a baseline of 0.636 lets precision fall to about 0.29 before the eval gate fails, so the regression gate is very weak.
finding.suggested_fix: Tighten the precision margin after more repeats give a stable spread.
finding.explanation: A wide margin lets a large drop in review quality pass the gate unnoticed.

first.rationale: The arithmetic is right (0.636 - 0.35 is about 0.29). But the margin is a deliberate choice that follows the README's documented procedure, and the README's own example gives 0.35. The description also says the margins are kept "as before", so this PR didn't introduce them. The finding is labelled "security", which is the wrong category.

quotes: const within = (drop: number | null, margin: number): boolean =>
For example, a precision with mean 0.667 and min 0.5 has a spread of 0.167. Twice the spread is 0.333, so the margin is 0.35.
escalated.rationale: The arithmetic is right: 0.636 − 0.35 ≈ 0.29. But the README rule for margins (twice the spread, kept at least 0.05 below the baseline) produces 0.35, and the PR says it chose this value on purpose. The finding is also not a security issue, and its suggested fix only defers the work until more repeats are run, so the post adds little.
